title: Netanyahu Calls October 7 'Darkest Day in Israel's History' in UN General Assembly Speech, Faces Walkouts and Effigy Protest
detail: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, addressing the UN General Assembly in New York on Thursday, September 24, 2026, described October 7, 2023 as 'the darkest day in Israel's history,' saying Hamas terrorists went house to house shooting Israeli civilians point-blank 'with fiendish glee and sadistic joy' while livestreaming the killings. He said 'our enemies expected us to collapse. Instead, we rose and fought like lions,' citing military gains against Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran over the three years since the attack, and said continuing violence against Israelis — particularly in the West Bank — goes uncovered by international media. Delegates staged a walkout as his speech began, prompting Netanyahu to invite any remaining 'moral cowards' to leave; outside the UN, protesters hanged a Netanyahu effigy in a noose and chanted 'Netanyahu in a bunker, we will put you six feet under.'

media.caption: Netanyahu addresses the UN General Assembly, calling October 7 'the darkest day in Israel's history,' September 24, 2026

title: IDF Probe Finds Paga Outpost ('Magen Be'eri') Was Unprepared for October 7, Opening Door to Be'eri Massacre
detail: The IDF released a probe on Thursday, September 24, 2026 finding that the Paga Outpost — officially named 'Magen Be'eri' ('Defender of Be'eri') — failed in its mission to defend the area and did not prevent Hamas from overrunning it on October 7, 2023, opening the way for the massacre at neighboring Kibbutz Be'eri. The probe found the combat team posted there had never drilled for a large-scale, simultaneous border infiltration, and cited seven systemic failures: hundreds of terrorists infiltrating through multiple routes overwhelmed defenders; soldiers were focused on minor perimeter disturbances rather than large-scale attack scenarios; the unit lacked sufficient preparedness despite adequate infrastructure; terrorist infiltration neutralized defensive and intelligence systems; enemy forces destroyed critical sector defenses; Israeli Air Force strikes were largely ineffective due to coordination gaps with ground forces; and commander casualties during the battle compromised decision-making. In total, 22 soldiers including officers were killed and 18 wounded in action at the outpost, and two soldiers were taken hostage to Gaza. 'The combat team posted at the outpost was not sufficiently prepared for such a terrorist infiltration,' the probe concluded.

media.caption: IDF probe finds the Paga Outpost ('Magen Be'eri') was unprepared to defend against the October 7 infiltration

title: Gaza Border Region Population Surpasses Pre-October 7 Levels by 10%, Tekuma Directorate Reports
detail: Israel's government Tekuma Directorate reported on Thursday, September 24, 2026 that the population of the Gaza border region (Tekuma area) has reached approximately 66,000 residents — about 10%, or roughly 5,000 people, above the pre-October 7, 2023 level of about 62,000 — with more than 90% of evacuated residents having returned and new families moving in, a growth rate the directorate said is 2.5 times the national average. Return rates vary by community: Kissufim has seen over 96% of residents return, Holit's returns began in late August, Kfar Aza's are expected in late September, and Be'eri's are expected between December 2026 and July 2027. The Tekuma Directorate, established October 19, 2023 under the Prime Minister's Office, has overseen a NIS 17 billion long-term recovery plan (including NIS 880 million for security, NIS 1 billion for education, and NIS 466 million for healthcare through end-2025) with a stated goal of doubling the region's population by 2033. 'Our mission is to create the conditions that will allow the region to continue rehabilitating, growing, and attracting new residents,' said Tekuma Directorate head Aviad Friedman.

media.caption: Families from Kibbutz Nir Oz, whose homes burned in the October 7 massacre, visit before reconstruction; the Gaza border region's population now exceeds pre-Oct. 7 levels
